low.symptoms: Yellowing of older leaves, stunted growth, pale green color
low.dosage: Apply Urea @ 100–120 kg/ha or FYM @ 10–15 tonnes/ha
low.timing: Apply in 2–3 splits — at sowing, knee-high, and flowering stage
low.tip: Avoid applying excess nitrogen as it promotes vegetative growth at expense of yield

optimal.symptoms: Plants show healthy green color and normal growth
fertilizers: Maintain with Urea or Ammonium Sulphate as per crop need
optimal.dosage: Maintain current levels. Apply recommended dose for specific crop
optimal.timing: Split application during crop growth stages
optimal.tip: Monitor regularly and adjust based on crop response and leaf color

high.symptoms: Dark green leaves, excessive vegetative growth, delayed maturity, lodging
organic: Avoid high-nitrogen manures like poultry manure
high.dosage: Skip nitrogen application for next 1–2 seasons
high.timing: Resume only after soil test confirms normal levels
high.tip: Excess nitrogen increases pest and disease susceptibility. Improve drainage to leach excess.

low.symptoms: Purple or reddish discoloration of leaves, poor root development, delayed maturity
low.dosage: Apply SSP @ 375 kg/ha or DAP @ 100 kg/ha
low.timing: Apply entire dose as basal before sowing — phosphorus is immobile in soil
low.tip: Apply near root zone for better uptake. Mycorrhizal inoculants improve phosphorus absorption.

optimal.symptoms: Good root development, healthy flowering and fruiting
fertilizers: Maintain with SSP or DAP as per crop requirement
optimal.dosage: Apply as per crop-specific recommended dose
optimal.tip: Phosphorus availability decreases in very acidic or alkaline soils. Maintain pH 6–7 for best uptake.

high.symptoms: Induced zinc and iron deficiency, reduced micronutrient availability
organic: Avoid bone meal and rock phosphate
high.timing: Resume after soil test shows normal levels
high.tip: Excess phosphorus locks out zinc and iron. Apply zinc sulphate to correct induced micronutrient deficiency.

low.symptoms: Scorching or burning of leaf tips and margins, weak stems, poor fruit quality
low.timing: Split application — half at sowing, half at flowering
low.tip: Potassium improves drought tolerance, disease resistance, and fruit quality. Do not skip for fruit crops.

optimal.symptoms: Strong stems, good fruit size, disease-resistant plants
fertilizers: Maintain with MOP or SOP as per crop requirement
optimal.dosage: Apply recommended dose for specific crop
optimal.tip: Potassium requirement increases at fruiting stage. Increase dose slightly for fruit crops.

high.symptoms: Induced magnesium and calcium deficiency, salt stress in sensitive crops
high.timing: Resume after soil test confirms reduction
high.tip: Flush soil with excess irrigation to reduce potassium buildup. Monitor calcium and magnesium levels.

acidic.symptoms: Aluminum and manganese toxicity, poor nutrient availability, reduced microbial activity
acidic.dosage: Apply lime @ 2–4 tonnes/ha depending on soil texture and target pH
acidic.timing: Apply 2–4 weeks before sowing to allow reaction with soil
acidic.tip: Dolomite lime also supplies magnesium. Re-test soil pH after 3 months. Avoid over-liming.

optimal.symptoms: All nutrients are most available, good microbial activity
optimal.dosage: No amendment needed. Maintain with compost
optimal.timing: Regular organic matter addition keeps pH stable
optimal.tip: Maintain pH 6–7 for most crops. Regular compost addition buffers pH naturally.

alkaline.symptoms: Iron, zinc, manganese deficiency, poor nutrient uptake, chlorosis
alkaline.dosage: Apply elemental sulphur @ 500–1000 kg/ha or gypsum @ 2–3 tonnes/ha
alkaline.tip: Foliar spray of iron and zinc sulphate corrects immediate deficiency symptoms while soil amendment takes effect.
